SMTO-ART-0014 — SMTO got an unusable reply while saving files

GUID: 1654691f-6b08-4a32-a045-85d17dfae9d4
Slug: artifact-protocol-invalid
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • While saving files from a Task, SMTO got a reply from the Gateway (the helper program that runs commands on a computer) that it couldn't use, or no proper reply at all. The files weren't saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for the Gateway this Task used. If the Gateway is offline or its connection broke, SMTO can't get a usable reply from it.
  2. Select Check for updates below the Gateway list. If that Gateway then shows an Update to button, select it when no important work is running there. A Gateway from a different release can reply in a form this SMTO server doesn't understand.
  3. Open Artifacts from this run and select Retry collection if it appears. Once the Gateway replies properly, SMTO collects the files the Task left behind.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway connection check succeeds and the files appear in Artifacts from this run.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't install an older or different Gateway build over the current one; use the update offered for your server's release.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Artifact metadata failed validation (workspace environment, snapshot, temp staging, chunk or status fields), or a Gateway artifact operation failed with an unexpected HTTP error, connection error or oversized/invalid response.

What this means

  • Artifact validation rejects workspace/snapshot/status/chunk metadata, while generic Gateway operation wrappers also classify unhandled transport/status failures under the artifact protocol family. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Artifact validation rejects workspace/snapshot/status/chunk metadata, while generic Gateway operation wrappers also classify unhandled transport/status failures under the artifact protocol family.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact metadata/transport stage and safe status; this broad category does not prove the caller fabricated data.

How to fix it

  • Find the diagnostic in the collection status or Server log: malformed workspace, snapshot, staging or chunk metadata usually means Gateway/server version skew, while 'Artifact Gateway operation failed' means the Gateway call itself failed (check reachability and the Gateway log). Align Gateway and server releases, confirm connectivity, then retry collection; never fabricate snapshot or receipt values.
  • Refresh the owning workspace through the supported publication flow and inspect Gateway version compatibility. Do not synthesize receipt or snapshot values.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported owning flow returns complete consistent metadata and trustworthy publication evidence.

What not to do

  • Do not overwrite the original state with an incompatible version; use the supported upgrade path.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
